pub const SCHEMA: [&str; 3] = [
    "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS evals (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(name) > 0),
        workspace TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(name),
        base TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(base) >= 7),
        created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)",
    // One row per rung an arm sets. `stage` is set only for a capability.
    "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS eval_arms (
        eval TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evals(id),
        arm TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (arm IN ('a','b')),
        kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('constraint','capability')),
        target TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(target) > 0),
        stage TEXT CHECK (stage IS NULL OR stage IN ('plan','approve','build','review','land')),
        rung TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (rung IN ('told','checked','enforced','denied','ask','allowed')))",
    "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS eval_runs (
        eval TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evals(id),
        arm TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (arm IN ('a','b')),
        idx INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (idx >= 0),
        request TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(request) > 0),
        job TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES jobs(id),
        grade INTEGER CHECK (grade IS NULL OR grade BETWEEN 0 AND 10),
        PRIMARY KEY (eval, arm, idx))",
];

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
O exit fixes: turns keep every stage's usage; dark decisions log in order

- `turns` still checked for the short pipeline's stages only, so no
  full-pipeline turn kept its usage. It moves to the staged tables, and
  migration 2 rebuilds it on a server that already ran migration 1.
- A dark step's decision is noted before the next effects are spawned,
  so the audit log keeps the order the steps went on in.
EOF
cargo build -p bastion-server --release 2>&1 | tail -1; pkill -f "target/release/bastion-server"; sleep 2; lsof -nP -iTCP:49190 -sTCP:LISTEN || echo free

864:| K | done | Added 2026-11-06 (D34). K1, spike N13, passes (docs/levels.md): an Anthropic key imported from the login shell into the `secrets` vault, readable only by `llm-router`, and referenced as `secret://ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the router's entry, ran a plan turn with no key in the stack's environment. `providers.openai.api_url` reaches one Chat Completions host in place of OpenAI, embeddings included, so K3 still needs its own worker. K2: `GET /providers` lists each provider and where its key comes from (`secret`, `env` or `none`), never the key; `PUT` and `DELETE /providers/{id}/key` keep a key in the vault as `<ID>_API_KEY`, readable only by `llm-router`, and set or clear `secret://` in the router's entry, keeping the rest of the entry; an unknown provider stores nothing. Settings has a Model providers section with a field and Set per provider, and Remove for a key set there; Accounts no longer lists providers. Doctor passes when any provider has a key and fails only when none has. The stack gained `provider-deepseek` 0.1.24, `provider-xai` 1.3.23, `provider-zai` 0.5.18, `provider-kimi` 1.1.19 and `provider-openrouter` 0.1.16, each the newest in the train of the pinned router; the registry has no Google, Mistral, Groq, Together, Fireworks, Ollama or Qwen worker. Live: all seven providers ready, Anthropic's vault key kept across a stack restart, a dummy xAI key set and removed through the API. 94 core, 95 server tests. Then the subscriptions: `provider-openai-codex` 0.4.30 and `provider-claude-code` 0.1.25 (0.2.x needs iii 0.26, and this stack runs 0.25). `llm-router` reports both as having no credential, so the server asks each itself and lists it as `signed_in`: Codex by its `auth::status`, Claude Code by whether its catalog has models. OpenAI Codex signs in with a ChatGPT plan from Settings, by a device code the page polls until it ends (`/providers/openai-codex/sign-in`, `/sign-in/poll`, `/sign-out`), and the worker reads its models again after. Claude Code reads the sign-in of `claude` on the stack's machine (Keychain), so Settings reports it and says how to sign in there. A key for either is refused. The stage model pickers offer every provider with a key or a sign-in. Live: Claude Code signed in through the Keychain with 12 models offered; the Codex sign-in returned a link and a code. 97 server tests. A plan turn on `claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5` reached Approve. K3 is deferred until after O, W and A8, built in full then; K4 is met by the stage pickers offering every provider with a key or a sign-in. Found live: a provider reads its models only at start, so a new key offered no models; setting or removing a key now asks `provider::<id>::refresh_models`. Exit, live (2026-11-06): with no Anthropic or DeepSeek key in the stack's environment, both keys went to the vault through `secrets::import` from the login shell (the same vault entry and router reference the Settings route writes, which a dummy xAI key exercised end to end), and plan turns on `claude-haiku-5-5` (Anthropic), `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek) and `claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5` (Claude Code through the Keychain) each reached Approve. Not shown: a key typed into the Settings page itself, and a Codex sign-in, as the owner has no Codex account. OpenAI and Z.AI keys are still in the stack's environment. 97 server tests. K is done except K3, deferred. |

The `bastion-server` binary takes `--checkout`, `--data`, `--port` and `--engine`, keeps its token in `data/token` (mode 0600), starts or attaches to the stack, and serves on loopback. Live (2026-11-06) against the second stack: the server started the stack, opened the store on the third try once `database` registered, ran migration 1 through the worker (`user_version` 1, the seed's 5 constraints and 3 grants), refused a request with no token, answered `/engine`, `/jobs` and `/constraints`, pushed a change on `/events` when a preset was set, answered a stale `Last-Event-ID` with `resync`, refused a bad preset with 400, and stopped the stack through `/stack/stop`. 86 core, 77 server, 3 app tests (62ea1a5). S3, the view on the API: the page sends each server command over HTTP by a route table in `bastion-protocol` (a server test sends every row and fails on a 404 or 405), with the token from the window's `target` command, and follows `GET /events` with `fetch`, reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID`; a resync, a reconnect or the window's focus makes every page read again, the engine status included. The app keeps three commands (`profile`, `target`, `quit`), no longer links the server, and starts `bastion-server` in its own process group, or attaches to the one on port 49190. The page decides a quit: it asks only while the stack runs, and the server outlives the app. Live (2026-11-06), on the owner's stack after backing up `data/bastion.db`: the app started the local server, migration 1 ran through the `database` worker and kept the 15 jobs and 83 artifacts; the Jobs page showed them and the Engine page the link up; with the server killed the Link card said `Down: http://127.0.0.1:49190 does not answer.`, and after a restart the open page came back up with no reload; a relaunched app attached to the running server instead of starting another. Not confirmed: the quit question (after its close button, screenshots of the window came back blank), and ⌘Q quits without asking, as Tauri's Quit menu item exits with a code; a stale error stays on the stack card after an outage. The sidebar's server label is gone (D30). 86 core, 78 server, 3 app, 3 view, 1 protocol tests (8004bb8). S4, Bastion servers, built: the app keeps the servers the owner added in `servers.toml`, each token in the Keychain (`keyring`), with `local` always first; the page follows every server's events and calls any of them (`call_on`). The Jobs page lists every server's jobs, each row naming its server, and the filter offers each server and workspace that has jobs. New request picks a Bastion server, `local` by default, then one of its workspaces; opening a job makes its server the current one, and the job page names it. The pages about one server have a Bastion server picker at their top, and Settings lists the servers with add and remove. The `profile` command is gone from the page; `profiles.toml` only tells the app how to start `local`. 86 core, 78 server, 5 app, 3 view, 1 protocol tests (fe68813). Exit, live (2026-11-06), with `local` and a second Bastion server on a second stack on this machine: Two was added in Settings, its token went to the Keychain and not to `servers.toml`; New request on `local` with `demo-local` started `j7df1a6c2`, and New request with Two picked showed only Two's workspace and started `jcbf97e51`; the Jobs page listed both under their servers, and each reached Approve with one plan. Closing the window with the stack running asked the quit question (S3's open item), Keep it running quit the app with both servers and both stacks up, and the reopened app listed both jobs where they were. Killing only Two's server left its stack running, and the restarted server attached to it. Found, and open: the Jobs page does not say when a server cannot be reached, and keeps showing its last read; stopping the background task that ran Two's server took its stack down too, and the job waiting at Approve lost its VM (`sandbox not found` at stop), so a job that waits across a stack restart cannot go on; whether a plan turn survives a kill mid-turn is not shown, because the plan finished too fast to tell; the add-server form keeps its values after Add. Then the Jobs page's unreachable server: the page now marks a server whose event stream is down, names it above the list, keeps that server's jobs as last read and marks them unreachable, and still says why a reachable server's jobs did not read; checked live by killing only Two's server, which put up the note, and restarting it, which cleared the note and brought Two's job back with no reload. content.content:
71e2da3 Plan: O done, with its live exit and what it did not show
647:#### W — Workflows on a canvas (L)
#### W — Workflows on a canvas (L)

**Goal:** a person picks a workflow for a request, and an admin edits
workflows as an interactive flow chart on a canvas (D35).

**Steps:**

- **W1, the model.** A workflow is a named graph of steps, each with its
  oversight dial (D33), kept on the Bastion server with its versions. The
  default workflows ship with the server and cannot be deleted, only
  copied.
- **W2, the canvas.** A Workflows page draws a workflow as a flow chart:
  add, remove, connect and reorder steps, and set each step's dial. Only an
  admin edits (D31); everyone else sees it read-only.
- **W3, picking one.** New request picks a workflow, the server's default
  first; the job page draws the job's workflow with its progress.

**Exit, live:** an admin copies a default workflow, drops a step on the
canvas and saves it; a member runs a request on the copy and the job skips
that step; a viewer sees the workflow but cannot edit it.

#### A8 — The full pipeline (L)

**Goal:** a job can run wipp's whole factory.

- Every stage wipp has, with its person checkpoints:
  - Shape: provision, prepare, scope, discover, clarify (person), plan,
    approve (person).
  - Acceptance tests: define, your checks (person), specify, baseline (the
    tests must fail first), falsify.
  - Build: implement (one turn per plan item, tests first), checks, refactor
    with the owner's pick, acceptance, review with the owner's pick.
  - Ship: ship (commit, push, PR), CI, CI fix, prove, comprehend (the
    briefing), UAT (person), merge (person), deploy (watch CD), learn,
    teardown.
  - Side paths: onboard, revive.
- Split a job into parts that depend on each other. The Jobs page shows parts
  under their job.
- Read-only stages get a read-only grant. A changed tree in one is reverted.
- The owner picks a pipeline per request, and sets the dial per checkpoint.

131:| D35 | A pipeline is a workflow: a flow chart of steps that a person edits on a canvas. Bastion ships a few workflows, and people make their own for themselves and others to use. For now only an admin makes or changes a workflow; members and viewers use them. | The owner's choice (2026-11-06). |

p='PLAN.md'; s=open(p).read()
def rep(a,b):
    global s
    assert s.count(a)==1, a[:70]
    s=s.replace(a,b)
rep("| D35 | A pipeline is a workflow: a flow chart of steps that a person edits on a canvas. Bastion ships a few workflows, and people make their own for themselves and others to use. For now only an admin makes or changes a workflow; members and viewers use them. |",
"| D35 | A pipeline is a workflow: a graph of steps that a person edits on a canvas. Each node is a step: what runs, its oversight dial (D33), a note that the node expands to show and that the step's agent reads, and the results it declares, such as documents, kept in the database. A link sends one step's results to another. Links carry no conditions: a step's entry criteria are the results of the steps linked into it, and its exit criteria are the results it declares, and a code check, not a model, holds a step that lacks either. Bastion ships a few workflows, and people make their own for themselves and others to use. For now only an admin makes or changes a workflow; members and viewers use them. |")
i=s.index("- **W1, the model.**"); j=s.index("#### A8 — The full pipeline (L)")
s=s[:i]+"""- **W1, the model.** A workflow is a graph, kept on the Bastion server
  with its versions. A node is a step (stage, dial, note, the results it
  declares, its place on the canvas); a link joins two nodes, and the later
  one gets the earlier one's results. The graph has no cycle, each stage at
  most once, and one node that lands the change (land or merge) with only
  deploy and learn after it. Only an agent step declares results. A job
  keeps the version it started on and runs the nodes in link order, ties
  broken by the canvas, skipping every stage the graph does not have.
  Before a step: each result linked into it exists, or the job waits on a
  person. After a turn: its report gives each declared result as a
  `RESULT <name>:` section, kept as a document; a missing one is one more
  try with the reason, then a wait on a person. The built-in workflows
  (short, full, full without acceptance tests) are chains with no results
  and the settings' dials; they cannot be changed or deleted, only copied.
- **W2, the canvas.** A Workflows page draws each workflow's nodes and
  links. An admin (D31) drags a node, links two by dragging from one to the
  other, removes a node or a link, adds a step from a palette, and expands
  a node to set its dial, note and results; saving makes a new version.
  Everyone else sees it read-only.
- **W3, picking one.** New request picks a workflow, the server's default
  first. The job page draws the job's workflow with each step's state, and
  each result as its document.

**Exit, live:** an admin copies a default workflow, removes a step, gives
plan a `design-notes` result linked into build, and saves; a member runs a
request on the copy; the job skips the removed step, the design notes are
kept as a document and reach the build's brief; a viewer sees the workflow
but cannot edit it.

"""+s[j:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git commit -qam "Plan: workflows are graphs of steps linked by results, with entry and exit criteria and no conditions (D35, W)" && git push -q 2>&1 | tail -1

lines: | D32 | A Bastion server listens on loopback unless its admin gives it an address and a TLS certificate and key; it refuses a non-loopback address without them. | A token sent over plain HTTP can be read by anyone on the network. |

| D33 | Every step of a pipeline is lights-on (it waits for a person to approve its result or send it back with feedback) or dark (it goes on at once). Every step starts lights-on, and each can be set on its own, merge included. A workflow's level follows from its steps: lights-on when every step has a person's gate, dim when at least one step up to the merge has one, and dark when none up to the merge has one (no human oversight of what merges). No step waits on a timer. The checkpoint stages fold into the steps they judge, and merge is a step that merges. Oversight decides only human approval and feedback: every step's result is kept, and every decision is logged, whatever the dial. A person's decisions are in the audit log with their name, and a dark step's decision is there too, named as the dial's. Replaces D15. | The owner's choice (2026-11-06): the factory runs the whole pipeline, and the amount of oversight is the variable. A step is governed by a person or runs alone; a timer that approves by itself governs nothing. |

| D34 | Model provider keys are configuration, not environment. Bastion stores each key in the stack's `secrets` worker (store `vault`, readable only by `llm-router`) and points the router's provider entry at it as `secret://NAME`; the router resolves it at each request and reports whether a provider has a key without returning it. Providers with their own worker (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, xAI, Z.AI for GLM, Kimi, OpenRouter) take their key that way; other OpenAI-compatible hosts (Together, Fireworks, Qwen through DashScope, a local Ollama) go through a Bastion provider worker that serves any number of them. | The owner's choice (2026-11-06): a key for any provider, with a spread wide enough that most people can use it, and no dependency on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment. |

-| D35 | A pipeline is a workflow: a flow chart of steps that a person edits on a canvas. Bastion ships a few workflows, and people make their own for themselves and others to use. For now only an admin makes or changes a workflow; members and viewers use them. | The owner's choice (2026-11-06). |

+| D35 | A pipeline is a workflow: a graph of steps that a person edits on a canvas. Each node is a step: what runs, its oversight dial (D33), a note that the node expands to show and that the step's agent reads, and the results it declares, such as documents, kept in the database. A link sends one step's results to another. Links carry no conditions: a step's entry criteria are the results of the steps linked into it, and its exit criteria are the results it declares, and a code check, not a model, holds a step that lacks either. Bastion ships a few workflows, and people make their own for themselves and others to use. +  one gets the earlier one's results. The graph has no cycle, each stage at
+  most once, and one node that lands the change (land or merge) with only
+  deploy and learn after it. Only an agent step declares results. A job
+  keeps the version it started on and runs the nodes in link order, ties

+  Before a step: each result linked into it exists, or the job waits on a

input.command:
cargo clippy --workspace --exclude bastion-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings 2>&1 | grep -cE "^(error|warning)"; cargo test --workspace --exclude bastion-ui 2>&1 | grep "test result" | awk '{s+=$4; f+=$6} END {print s" passed, "f" failed"}'; git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
W1: workflows are graphs of steps linked by results

- The core's workflow graph: nodes (stage, dial, note, declared results,
  place on the canvas) and links. Its check: each stage once, no circle,
  links between its own nodes, results only on agent steps and named once,
  one node that lands with only deploy and learn after it. Its order: link
  order, ties left to right on the canvas.
- A job keeps its workflow's steps and the results they gave. Before a
  step, each result linked into it must exist, or the job waits on a
  person. After a turn, each declared result must be a `RESULT <name>:`
  section: one more try with the reason, then a wait. Linked results, and
  the node's note, go into the step's brief. A fix loop's return to a step
  the workflow left out goes on to the next step it has.
- The server keeps workflows as versions (nodes, results, links); a job
  keeps the version it started on, and runs under its dials. The built-in
  workflows are the pipelines as chains under the settings' dials; they can
  be copied, not saved or deleted. A job's results are kept as documents.
- `GET /workflows`, `POST /workflows` (copy), `PUT /workflows/{id}` (a new
  version), `DELETE /workflows/{id}`; a request can name a workflow.
EOF
git push -q 2>&1 | tail -1
